summary: The servlet's bad() entry point calls System.exit(1), which terminates the entire JVM (and thus the servlet container) when the request handler runs — the CWE-382 unsafe sink. In a servlet/J2EE context, terminating the VM must never happen. I replaced the System.exit(1) call with a plain return so the handler cleanly finishes the request without killing the container. The method's control flow (the if-block structure and request handling path) is preserved; valid requests still complete normally.
